text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Around 260 awaiting trial prisoners are being held in state prisons where they are treated in similar ways to convicted prisoners, prompting a call for a review of the judicial system in line with the right to a trial within reasonable time -- as enshrined in the constitution.
- Finance Minister Nangolo Mbumba is expected to focus on Namibia's medium term economic goals such as social and industrial development when he introduces the 1997/98 budget.

- The government is planning to change the law governing municipal councils, to provide for local elections in December to be held on a party list system rathern than in wards. It is intended increase the number of women in decision-making positions.

- Information and Broadcasting Permanent Secretary Nguno Wakolele has warned Namibian journalists against complacency. He said they must be aware that the constitution could be amended at any time if the right to the freedom of expression was being abused.
